acceptance.given: A Toolchain TC-D1 change proposes writing to a runtime boundary path.

oracle.expected: The write attempt is rejected and the runtime boundary remains protected.
forbidden: Replay or Consumer permission is treated as authorization for runtime repair.
oracle.observable: The validator or write guard emits a deterministic rejection tied to the runtime-boundary target and no runtime file mutation is observed.

acceptance.then: The proposed write is rejected without changing any runtime boundary file.
acceptance.when: During validation of the TC-D1 write set, the attempted target resolves to a runtime boundary path.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the runtime-boundary write-rejection test against a target under the runtime path and verify the guard observes that exact target.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject TC-D1 writes targeting runtime boundaries; preserve runtime files and do not infer authorization from replay or Consumer permissions.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema or runtime-state changes; restoring the prior replay implementation restores write-set behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: proposed runtime-boundary write -> deterministic rejection -> unchanged runtime boundary
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator reports rejection for the runtime target and a before/after content check shows no runtime boundary mutation.

acceptance.given: An aggregate execution is launched through bounded Toolchain process controls.

oracle.expected: The aggregate reaches one deterministic terminal category within the configured time and output bounds.
forbidden: The aggregate ends indeterminate or nondeterministically.
Budget exhaustion is reported as success.
A timeout or output overflow silently reduces required coverage.
oracle.observable: The aggregate receipt records bounded execution facts and exactly one terminal category that can be reproduced by the selector.

acceptance.then: The run is classified with a deterministic terminal state and bounded outcome; budget exhaustion is unsuccessful.
acceptance.when: After each aggregate execution terminates or reaches its configured timeout/output limit, the runtime receipt and terminal classifier are inspected.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the bounded aggregate test with a deterministic completion case and assert the runtime terminal marker is emitted and stable.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce bounded time/output for aggregate processes and classify every termination deterministically, treating exhaustion as unsuccessful.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing receipt categories and bounded-process interfaces; reverting these files restores prior execution behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: aggregate running -> bounded completion/timeout classification -> deterministic terminal category
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The aggregate receipt contains one terminal category, timeout/output limits are enforced, and repeated selector runs produce the same classification for identical pinned inputs.

acceptance.given: An always-success false-negative condition is supplied to the detached Probe evaluator.

oracle.expected: The Probe outcome is failed and identifies the always-success false-negative condition.
forbidden: The Probe passes the always-success false negative.
The condition is treated as infrastructure success or omitted from the result.
oracle.observable: The independent Probe process returns a failed outcome with a diagnostic identifying the always-success false-negative condition.

acceptance.then: The evaluator records a failed Probe result for the always-success false negative.
acceptance.when: The detached Probe executes with bound input/output evidence and its result is classified.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the Probe evaluation selector with an always-success false-negative fixture and verify the contract-level failure classification.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Detect and fail always-success false negatives during independent Probe evaluation while preserving bound inputs and outputs.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema change; reverting the Probe evaluator owners restores prior classification behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: always-success false-negative presented -> independent Probe execution -> failed Probe outcome
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The Probe receipt binds the tested input and process output and reports failure for the always-success false-negative case.

acceptance.given: An aggregate is evaluated with matrix evidence whose label does not match the executed case or fixture.

oracle.expected: The aggregate is marked invalid and cannot be accepted.
forbidden: The aggregate remains valid or is accepted despite mislabeled matrix evidence.
Relabeling is treated as execution evidence.
oracle.observable: Aggregate evaluation emits an invalid verdict with a mislabeled-evidence diagnostic and blocks acceptance.

acceptance.then: The aggregate remains invalid and acceptance publication is blocked.
acceptance.when: Matrix evidence identity, fixture/state transition, and declared case label are reconciled during aggregate evaluation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the matrix aggregate validator with a deliberately mislabeled evidence record and assert rejection of the aggregate.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Invalidate aggregates when matrix evidence labels do not match the executed case, fixture, or state transition; prevent acceptance of the invalid aggregate.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing matrix and receipt schemas; reverting the replay owner restores prior aggregate evaluation behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: mislabeled matrix evidence supplied -> identity/label reconciliation -> aggregate invalidation
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The aggregate result is invalid, contains the mislabeled-evidence diagnostic, and cannot transition to an accepted state.
